info.name: Food Manager API
info.description: Device-key (passkey-style) auth backend for the Food Manager app. Run requests top-to-bottom within a folder — each request's test script auto-fills variables the next request needs (username, keys, tokens, ids). The 'Dev Helpers' calls (/api/dev/keypair, /api/dev/sign) stand in for the Android Keystore and are only mounted when NODE_ENV != production.

request.description: Dev-only helper standing in for the Android Keystore. Generates an Ed25519 keypair.
Checks availability of the freshly-generated username before it has been registered — expects available: true. Sets the collectionVariable 'username' that 1.2 Register reuses.
Same username as 1.2 Register, now that it's taken — expects available: false.
Dev-only helper: signs the nonce with the device's private key, exactly like the Android Keystore would.
Rotates the refresh token — old one is revoked, so run this once per test pass.

exec: // Reuses the last challengeId/deviceId but sends garbage as the signature.

request.description: Negative test: run 1.3 (Challenge) again first to get a fresh, unused challengeId, then this request.

Works right after registration (register already returns an accessToken) or any time later to add/change the email on file. After sending, check the running server's console output for two lines: '[email] Link: .../email/verify?token=...' and '[email] Code: 123456' — either one confirms the same pending email. Paste the token into emailVerificationToken (for 2.2) or the code into emailVerificationCode (for 2.3).
Requires emailVerificationToken to be set manually from the server console log (see 2.1). Alternative to 2.3 — either verifies the same pending email, whichever is used first invalidates the other.

Requires emailVerificationCode to be set manually from the server console log (see 2.1) — a 6-digit code as an alternative to clicking the link in 2.2, for clients that can't open a deep link. Verifies the most recent pending email for the authenticated user. The code expires after EMAIL_CODE_TTL seconds (default 10 min) and locks out after EMAIL_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS wrong guesses (default 5) — request a fresh one via 2.1 if that happens.

Only actually sends a recovery email if the account has a VERIFIED email on file (run 2.1 + 2.2 first). Response is always the same generic message either way — check the server console for the real recovery link/token, then paste it into the recoveryToken collection variable.
Requires recoveryToken to be set manually from the server console log (see 4.1).

Login by username + email — the fallback path a client should only try after /challenge + /verify (1.3-1.5) fails (lost/reset device, fresh install, etc.). Only actually sends a code when that username has a VERIFIED email on file that matches the one sent (run 2.1 + 2.2/2.3 first so {{username}}_updated@example.com is verified). The response is always the same generic message either way (anti-enumeration). The code is only ever mailed to the account's on-file address, never to an arbitrary one. Check the running server's console for '[email] Code: 123456' and paste it into the recoveryCode collection variable for 4.6.
A fresh keypair for the code-login device. confirm-code (4.6) registers this public key as a new device, so it must not already be registered — don't reuse the recovery device from 4.2.

Completes login by username + email: verifies the emailed code (set recoveryCode from the console — see 4.4), registers the new device public key from 4.5, and returns { user, device, accessToken, refreshToken } — the client is now logged in on this device. The code is single-use, expires after RECOVERY_CODE_TTL seconds (default 10 min), and locks out after RECOVERY_CODE_MAX_ATTEMPTS wrong guesses (default 5); request a fresh one via 4.4 if that happens.

request.description: Negative test: same username + correct code as 4.6, but an email that does NOT match the account's verified on-file address. Must be rejected with 400 INVALID_RECOVERY_CODE and no session issued — a mismatched email must never let the client in. Run 4.4 again first to get a fresh, unused code if 4.6 already consumed it.
Returns the authenticated user's profile, including the current imageUrl (null when no picture is set).

Sets or changes the profile picture — idempotent, so run it again with a different profileImageUrl to change the image. imageUrl must be an http(s) URL (max 2048 chars). Returns the full updated profile.
Removes the profile picture (sets imageUrl back to null). Returns the full updated profile.

exec: pm.test('status was saved', () => pm.expect(body.user.status).to.eql('Hungry for good food'));
pm.test('description was saved', () => pm.expect(body.user.description).to.eql('I love trying new recipes.'));

request.description: Partial update of the editable profile fields. Send any non-empty subset of { username?, name?, age?, status?, description? } — only the fields present change. username is the unique login handle (3-20 chars, [a-zA-Z0-9_]); a value already taken by another account returns 409 USERNAME_TAKEN. For the text fields (name/status/description) send null (or "") to clear a field. Returns the full updated profile. To also test renaming, add a "username" field to the body.

Replaces the authenticated user's food preferences with the given list of free-form strings (e.g. ["spicy", "italian"]). Idempotent — the whole list is replaced every call, and an empty array [] clears it. Entries are trimmed, lowercased, de-duplicated, capped at 100 chars each and 100 entries total. Edit the 'foodPreferences' collection variable to change what's sent. Returns the full updated profile, whose foodPreferences array is sorted alphabetically.

Replaces the authenticated user's food exceptions — things they dislike / want avoided — with the given list of free-form strings (e.g. ["cilantro", "mushrooms"]). Same replace-in-full, idempotent semantics and validation as 6.1. Edit the 'foodExceptions' collection variable to change what's sent. Returns the full updated profile, whose foodExceptions array is sorted alphabetically.

exec: pm.test('diets is an array of enum codes', () => pm.expect(body.diets).to.be.an('array'));

request.description: Returns the fixed, server-owned diet catalog as an array of enum codes (e.g. ["VEGETARIAN", "VEGAN", ...]), ordered by the catalog's sortOrder. The client maps each code to a localized display name. This list is not user-editable; new diets are added server-side (future admin panel).

Replaces the authenticated user's selected diets with the given list of enum codes from the catalog (7.1) — e.g. ["VEGETARIAN", "VEGAN"]. Codes are upper-cased and de-duplicated; every code must exist in the catalog (an unknown code returns 400 UNKNOWN_DIET). Idempotent — the whole selection is replaced each call, and an empty array [] clears it. Edit the 'userDiets' collection variable to change what's sent. Returns the full updated profile, whose diets array is ordered like the catalog.

Returns the authenticated user's client-side settings { language, theme, pushNotificationsEnabled }. Every account gets a default set at registration ({ language: 'en', theme: 'SYSTEM', pushNotificationsEnabled: true }), so this works immediately after register/login. The same object is also embedded in GET /users/me (5.1).

Partial update of the authenticated user's settings — send any non-empty subset of { language, theme, pushNotificationsEnabled } and only those fields change. language is a BCP-47 tag (e.g. 'en', 'ru', 'en-US'); theme is one of LIGHT|DARK|SYSTEM; pushNotificationsEnabled is a boolean. An empty body, an unknown key, or an invalid value returns 400. Edit the settingsLanguage / settingsTheme / pushNotificationsEnabled collection variables to change what's sent. Returns the full updated settings.

exec: pm.test('cuisines is an array of enum codes', () => pm.expect(body.cuisines).to.be.an('array'));

request.description: Returns the fixed, server-owned cuisine catalog as an array of enum codes (e.g. ["ITALIAN", "JAPANESE", ...]), ordered by the catalog's sortOrder. The client maps each code to a localized display name. Same pattern as GET /diets. These codes are also what a client sends as reasonDetail for a WRONG_CUISINE dislike (see 10.6).

Dev-only helper (mounted only when NODE_ENV != production, like the keystore helpers). Seeds a fixed set of sample dishes — each with 1..7 images, per-serving nutrition, a cuisine and tag flags — so the feed has data. Idempotent: dishes have fixed UUIDs and are upserted, so re-running refreshes them in place. Run this once before exploring the feed.

The Tinder-style recommendation deck: a page of dishes the authenticated user has NOT swiped yet, newest first. Keyset (cursor) paginated — the response is { items, nextCursor, hasMore }. Each dish is fully shaped: { id, name, description, cuisine, images[] (1..7), nutrition { calories, servings, protein, fat, carbs }, tags { allergens[], dietaryRestrictions[], intolerances[], features[], diets[] }, createdAt, updatedAt }. limit is 1..50 (default 10). This test captures the first three dish ids (foodId/foodId2/foodId3) and the nextCursor for the requests below. Already-swiped dishes drop out of later pages automatically, so re-running after swiping returns fewer dishes.

The next page, using the opaque nextCursor captured by 10.1. Passing the cursor returns dishes that sort strictly after the last one seen — no overlap, no gaps, even as the swiped-set grows. A malformed cursor returns 400 INVALID_CURSOR. Run 10.1 first so feedCursor is set (if 10.1's page was the last one, feedCursor is empty and this just returns page 1 again).
Full detail for a single dish (same shape as a feed item). Uses the foodId captured by 10.1. A non-UUID id returns 400; an unknown (but well-formed) id returns 404 FOOD_NOT_FOUND.

Records the swipe verdict on a dish. Body: { action: "LIKE" | "SKIP" | "DISLIKE", reason?, reasonDetail? }. Idempotent per (user, dish) — re-swiping the same dish overwrites the previous verdict (so a SKIP can later become a LIKE). reason/reasonDetail are only allowed on DISLIKE (see 10.6); sending them here returns 400. After this, the liked dish no longer appears in the feed.
Skips a dish (the second one captured by 10.1). A SKIP is a neutral pass — the dish drops out of the feed like a like/dislike does, but carries no positive or negative preference signal.

'Hate it' with a reason (the third dish from 10.1). reason is one of DISLIKE_TAG | WRONG_CUISINE | ALREADY_ATE | ALLERGEN | NOT_IN_MOOD | OTHER. For DISLIKE_TAG send the tag code the user hates in reasonDetail (e.g. "SPICY", "MILK"); for WRONG_CUISINE send a cuisine code from GET /cuisines (e.g. "ITALIAN") — reasonDetail is required for those two and optional otherwise. These negative signals are what the future preference-based recommender learns from.

exec: pm.test('each entry carries the dish + verdict', () => body.items.forEach((i) => { pm.expect(i).to.have.property('action'); pm.expect(i.food).to.have.property('name'); }));

request.description: The authenticated user's own swipe history ('my likes / skips / dislikes'), newest first, keyset-paginated like the feed ({ items, nextCursor, hasMore }). Each item is { foodId, action, reason, reasonDetail, createdAt, updatedAt, food } where food is the full dish. Add ?action=LIKE|SKIP|DISLIKE to filter (see 10.8).

exec: pm.test('every entry is a LIKE', () => body.items.forEach((i) => pm.expect(i.action).to.eql('LIKE')));

request.description: The 'liked foods' screen: same list as 10.7 but filtered to LIKE. Swap the action query param for SKIP or DISLIKE to get those lists.

exec: pm.test('reports whether a verdict was removed', () => pm.expect(body.removed).to.be.a('boolean'));

request.description: Undo a swipe (Tinder-style rewind): removes the user's verdict on the dish so it re-enters the feed. Idempotent — returns { removed: true } if a verdict was cleared, { removed: false } if there was nothing to undo (never 404s).

Uploads a single image file (multipart field 'image': jpeg/png/webp/gif, max UPLOAD_MAX_FILE_SIZE_MB — 5MB by default) to local disk storage and returns its public URL as { imageUrl }. Select a file for the 'image' form-data field before sending. The client then sets that URL on whichever resource references it, e.g. PUT /users/me/image (5.2) — this request also copies the returned URL into the profileImageUrl collection variable so 5.2 can be run immediately after with the real uploaded file. An unsupported MIME type returns 400 UNSUPPORTED_IMAGE_TYPE, an oversized file returns 400 UPLOAD_LIMIT_FILE_SIZE, and a missing file returns 400 MISSING_FILE.
